title: Hyperbaric oxygen in the artificial intelligence era: integration and innovation

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Hyperbaric oxygen in the artificial intelligence era: integration and innovation》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · section-2-p1】Hyperbaric oxygen therapy (HBOT) administers 100% oxygen at elevated pressures, commonly 1.3 to 3.0 atmospheres absolute, thereby increasing the partial pressure of dissolved oxygen in plasma and steepening diffusion gradients across hypoxic tissue. Clinically, HBOT is a mainstay for decompression illness, arterial gas embolism, and carbon monoxide poisoning, and serves as an adjunct for difficult-to-heal wounds and late radiation tissue injury.12345 All HBOT dose bands are hypothesis-generating and not prescriptive; these are summarized in Tables 1–4.

【Introduction · section-2-p2】Over the past decade, research has probed potential benefits in neurological and inflammatory diseases, including post-concussive syndromes, stroke recovery, and inflammatory bowel disease.678 Across these domains, HBOT is thought to modulate inflammatory signaling, improve microvascular dynamics, and, in the central nervous system, and support neuroplastic remodeling.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Hyperbaric oxygen in the artificial intelligence era: integration and innovation》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Ethical, Regulatory, and Implementation Considerations · section-13-p1】Bias in training data can propagate inequities in access or outcomes. Ensuring representative datasets and auditing model performance across subgroups are minimum requirements for responsible HBOT-AI development.1220 Explainable AI should be embedded from the outset; interpretable models or post-hoc explanations enhance trust and ease regulatory review.1420 Regulators categorize AI that influences treatment parameters as high-risk Software as a Medical Device, requiring pre-market evidence, change-control plans, cybersecurity, and post-market surveillance.34 The evolving European AI Act adds horizontal obligations for transparency, risk management, and human oversight.35

【Search Methodology · section-3-p1】A structured literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar (January 2000–March 2025). We combined “hyperbaric oxygen therapy” (HBOT) with AI-related terms (“artificial intelligence,” “machine learning,” “deep learning,” “digital twin,” “biosensor*”). We included peer-reviewed English-language clinical, preclinical, or computational studies explicitly linking HBOT to AI or enabling technologies (e.g., wearable sensors used to inform algorithms). We excluded abstracts without full text, non-peer-reviewed sources, and editorials without data. Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses methodology was used. Results are presented in Figure 1.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Hyperbaric oxygen in the artificial intelligence era: integration and innovation》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusion · section-15-p1】Hyperbaric oxygen therapy has matured from a niche intervention to a versatile modality with clear benefits in several conditions. Yet practice remains constrained by protocol heterogeneity, limited real-time monitoring, and uncertain patient selection. The convergence with AI offers a coherent strategy to address these gaps: learn from multicenter data to optimize protocols; select patients through imaging-omic signatures; safeguard safety with predictive analytics; and progressively adapt therapy using biosensors and digital twins. Advancing toward precision HBOT will require hybrid clinical trials, interoperable registries, explainable and equitable models, and regulatory-grade validation. If pursued thoughtfully, the marriage of oxygen and algorithms can improve outcomes, reduce harms, and illuminate mechanisms of HBOT, transforming a largely empirical therapy into an adaptive, learning intervention. Accordingly, the dose bands proposed in this review are provisional and designed to be falsifiable through rigorous, regulator-aligned evaluation.

【Evolving Landscape of Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy · section-4-p2】Mechanistically, HBOT engages oxidative signaling, angiogenesis, and stem/progenitor cell mobilization; these effects, while biologically plausible, have not yet yielded reliable bedside biomarkers for selecting responders or titrating dose.678 The gap between mechanistic promise and clinical routine is precisely where AI can help: by learning from multi-modal data to personalize therapy and by enabling real-time adaptation during sessions.

【Ethical, Regulatory, and Implementation Considerations · section-13-p2】Methodological rigor also matters. Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 informs transparent synthesis of evidence.36 Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials-AI and Standard Protocol Items: Recommendations for Interventional Trials-AI extensions specify how to design and report clinical trials of AI-enabled interventions.3738 while DECIDE-AI provides a preclinical clinical-evaluation framework bridging development to trials.39 Continuous performance monitoring in real-world settings helps detect dataset shift and maintain safety.4041 Finally, reporting guidelines for prediction models (Transparent Reporting of a multivariable prediction model for Individual Prognosis Or Diagnosis) remain relevant when models are used to stratify HBOT candidates.42 Implementation roadmap is displayed in Figure 2.
